# Seed-1 results (AIME 2024)

Plateau window: steps 40-110. Model: Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B. Regenerate with

```bash
python3 scripts/seed1_table.py --git-ref origin/paper
```

> **One seed.** Every t below pairs the plateau *steps of one run*, so it
> measures whether a gap is stable inside one trajectory -- not whether it
> survives re-running, which is the question a reviewer asks. The eight
> points are consecutive validations of the same run and are not
> independent. `docs/preregistration_5seed.md` fixes the primary unit as the
> seed; at n=1 there is no seed-level test. **Do not quote these as the
> paper's significance.**

## What this does and does not show

* The ladder is `GRPO ~ STEER ~ uniform << STEER-F`. The three controls sit
  at zero and only the treatment moves. Shuffling A_H among siblings
  (permuted) removes most of the gain, which is what separates the signal
  from the apparatus that carries it.
* Most of the gain is not per-sample accuracy: uplift (maj - acc) carries
  the larger share of the majority-vote difference.
* Entropy is not the channel. The two arms whose plateau entropy is
  indistinguishable (STEER and STEER-F) are the two furthest apart in
  accuracy, and the arm with the highest entropy is not the best arm.
* **Not established.** One seed, one 30-problem benchmark. The only
  repeat we have of any arm (STEER-F run twice, common window 40-90)
  differed by .0088, against a headline gap of .0145 -- the same order of
  magnitude. The five-seed campaign is what decides this.

Also not in the table: the lambda=0 + tree arm (`train-Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B-s1-tree-rollout.log`) has a single validation point at step 110 (acc .1430), too few for a plateau. The H100 `lam0-tree` follow-up fills that cell.
